definitions: A financial position taken by an investor or trader who sells borrowed securities, commodities, or currencies with the expectation that their price will fall, allowing them to buy them back at a lower price and profit from the difference.
The state of having sold something that one does not own, with the intention of buying it back later at a lower price.
examples: He took a short position on the stock.
The hedge fund maintained a significant short position.
Closing a short position involves buying back the asset.
